chapter_theme: The history of the guru mathas (குரு மட வரலாறு): seven lines of teaching descend in the true path down to Mulan's own, and he spoke the Agama in nine tantras and three thousand verses; the second verse names founders of the lines.

101.reading: Of the seven mathas that came down in the abiding true path, up to Mulan's matha that arises first, he spoke the beautiful Agama in nine tantras, three thousand verses, as their support.
101.nuance: சன்மார்க்கம் (the true path) in Siddhanta is the path of knowledge. முந்தி உதிக்கின்ற (arising first) may mean Mulan's matha is the earliest or the foremost. The verse speaks of Mulan in the third person; the count of nine tantras and three thousand verses is the book's own.

102.reading: From Kalangar, who mingles in grace, came Aghorar, Maligai Devar who gives good, Nathantar, Paramanandar of keen insight and Bhoga Devar; the three who shine on earth are of Niramaya.
102.nuance: The verse lists founders or teachers of the mathas. Kalangar is likely the Kalangi of 69. மூவர் (the three) and நிராமயத்தோர் (those of Niramaya, or 'the flawless ones') are unclear, so the number and grouping of the names is not certain.

links.note: 69 names Kalangi among Tirumular's seven disciples; 102 makes Kalangar the head of a line through Aghorar and others, carrying the succession one generation further.

101 says Mulan spoke the Agama in nine tantras, three thousand verses (தந்திரம் ஒன்பது சார்வுமூவாயிரம்). 3046 counts the same work as three thousand Tamil verses, three hundred mantras and thirty teachings, and says the three are one (மூன்றும் ஒன்றாமே). The book's account of its own shape is extended from count to unity.

source_issues: 102: line 4 (நிலந்திகழ் மூவர் நிராமயத் தோரே) is unclear; the count of names does not obviously match seven mathas.
